segments.text: Good evening. This is Aakashwani. I am Valsa Williams with the news at 9.
The headlines. 11 crore pharma IDs created across the country five months ahead of March
2027 target to ensure transparent delivery of benefits under various schemes.
Center direct states and union territories to strictly prohibit reuse of single-use
medical devices and disposable surgical items in all health care facilities.
From Minister Narendra Modi to share his thoughts on his monthly radio program, Man Ki Baat,
on Akashwani tomorrow.

And in cricket, Inderbeat hosts New Zealand by four wickets in 2nd T20 International at Christchurch.
The government has created 11 crore pharma IDs across the country.
Five months ahead of the March 2027 deadline,
the milestone has been achieved under the Digital Agriculture Mission
implemented by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare.
Agriculture and farmers' well-feminist Shivraj Singh Johan said this in a video message on
social media.
Mr Johan said the target of creating 11 crore farmer IDs by March 2027 was set by Prime
Minister Narendra Modi and it was achieved yesterday.
The minister said the IDs will ensure transparent delivery of benefits under various government
schemes.
He said these IDs will also facilitate farmers in accessing bank loans, crop insurance, disaster
relief assistance, and selling their produce.
The initiative will help ensure that benefits reach the right farmers, but the use of modern
technology will make farming easier and more efficient.
I congratulate and thank the officials and employees of the central government as well
the State Government's union territories and district administrations for this achievement.
The Agriculture and Farmers Well Feminist, we said, the digital agriculture mission was
launched following the union cabinet's approval on the 2nd September 2024. It added that
through the pharma ID-based service delivery system, more than six crore farmers across the
have so far received direct benefits under various schemes.
Linking a verified pharma database with agricultural services
is helping eliminate fraud and the need for duplicate verification.
The Center has directed states and union territories
to strictly prohibit the reuse of single-use medical devices
and disposable surgical items in all public and private health care facilities.
In a letter to chief secretaries, health secretaries and directors of health services
of all states and UTs, DGHS said it has come to its notice that certain private and corporate
hospitals are reusing various single-use medical devices and disposable surgical items, particularly
in critical specialties such as cardiology, nephrology, oncology, cardiothoracic and
vascular surgery, neurosurgery and other specialized clinical services, more from our
correspondent.
DGHS has said that the practice of reusing single use devices and disposable surgical
items raises concerns relating to patient safety, infection prevention and control,
regulatory compliance and health care expenditure.
It has warned that this can also expose patients to significant risk including cross
infection, device malfunction, loss of performance, and other procedure-related complications.
DGHS has asked all states and union territories to ensure strict vigilance and effective enforcement
against the use of single-use medical devices and disposable surgical items, with Akshith
and Anand Rishu Jaiswal, Akashwani News, Delhi.
Union Minister of Science and Technology Dr. Jitendra Singh today inaugurated the
the Advanced Atmospheric Chemistry and Aerosol Toxicity Analysis Laboratory at IITM New Delhi.
The new laboratory is the world's first of its kind air pollution analysis facility for
Delhi NCR. The minister said Delhi NCR had been chosen in view of the serious public
concern over air pollution. He said the laboratory is equipped with advanced instruments
for analyzing the chemical composition of atmospheric gases and aerosols including fine
particulate matter, PM 2.5, metals, toxic elements and other components. It can further
distinguish metallic elements, microplastics or other carcinogenic elements present in the air
and send alerts to health authorities. The first facility of its kind in the world
has been installed today, a state-of-the-art facility. Mission Mossum was announced by
Prime Minister Narendra Modi for the first time this government has given this important
sector such high importance, which was not the case previously. The result of this is
that over the past 10 to 12 years, significant improvements have been made, firstly in
forecasting and alongside that in the analysis of air quality.
This is Aakashwani giving you the news.
Stay connected with AIR News, Follow us on X at AIRNewsAlerts and visit newsonair.gov.in
for the latest updates.
Welcome back here with us on the news at 9.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi will share his thoughts with the people of the country
and abroad in his monthly radio program Monkey Butt on Akashwani at 11am tomorrow. The program
will be broadcast across the entire Akashwani and Durdarshan network including AIR news website
and news on AIR mobile app. It will also be live streamed on the YouTube channels of AIR
news, DD news, the PMO and the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting. Immediately
after the broadcast of the program, Akashwani will broadcast the program in regional languages.
The BJP today hit out of the Congress party over its proposed rally on the first of next
months.
Briefing media at party headquarters senior BJP leader Ravi Shankar Prasad said the Chamber
of Trade and Industry in Delhi had written a letter to Congress leader and leader of
opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi to postpone the rally in the interest of traders.
The BJP leader alleged that Mr. Gandhi was unwilling to listen to the concerns of
ordinary citizens and traders.
The acting head of the state of Liechtenstein, Hereditary Prince Alua, will be on a four-day
visit to India from tomorrow. He is visiting India, the invitation of Prime Minister Narendra
Modi. He will be accompanied by his wife, Hereditary Princess Sophie, and a high level
of official as well as business delegation, comprising top industry leaders. During his
visit, Prime Minister Modi and Prince Alua will hold a bilateral meeting to discuss
cooperation in various areas, including trade and investment, science, technology and innovation,
and people-to-people exchanges, as well as exchange views on regional and global developments.
Prince Aloha will meet President Rabadi Murmur, who will also host an official banquet in
his honour.
In Varanasi, on the second day of the Wings Over Ganga air show, spectators witnessed
as the capabilities of the Indian Air Force.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi will witness the Air Force Day Aerial Display as the Chief
Guest at Namo Ghat tomorrow, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, and Defence
Minister Rajnath Singh will also be present on the occasion, a report.
The Aerial Display will feature aircraft including the Tejas, Light Combat Helicopter
Prachand SU-30 MKI and Rafale along with transport aircraft.
Aircraft from the Indian Navy and the Indian Army will also participate, showcasing jointness
in operations.
The Indian Air Force's premier display teams, including Suriya Kiran aerobatic team and
the Saring helicopter display team, will also participate in the event.
Before this, Prime Minister will inaugurate a new garment manufacturing facility in Varanasi.
The facility marks an important step towards extending India's textile and apparel manufacturing
ecosystem and promoting industrial growth in the region.
RLW Minister Ashwini Vaishnav today inaugurated Satna Devendra Nagarendriva Churhardt rail
sections under the Lalitpur Singh Roli railway project and flagged off the new Devendra Nagar
Churhardt passenger train service through videoconferencing.
Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Dr Mohan Yadav was present on the occasion.
India has condemned the attack at a church in Karak, Jordan, which took place yesterday.
Today, the attack resulted in the loss of several lives and injuries to many others.
External Affairs Minister Dr S.J. Shankar has expressed deep shock at the incident.
The Ministry of External Affairs said, India stands firmly with the government and people
of Jordan in this difficult hour.
New Delhi reaffirmed its commitment to the fight against terrorism in all its forms
and manifestations.
Airline operator Indigo has said its flights to and from four Saudi Arabian cities will
remain cancelled in view of the evolving security situation till the 31st of this month.
In a social media post, Indigo said its flights to and from Riyadh, Jadda, Damam and Madina
will remain cancelled till the 31st of this month.
The airline said the safety and well-being of customers and crew continue to guide their
decisions.
It added that they are in close coordination with the relevant authorities to ensure
safe operations.
A developing weather system over the Bay of Bengal is likely to intensify into a cyclonic
storm and approach the South Odisha North-Andhra Pradesh coast early next week.
The endometrological department has forecast heavy to extremely heavy rainfall in several
parts of Odisha from Tuesday.
The Odisha government has stepped up disaster preparedness more in this report.
According to the India Metallurgical Department, a well-marked low-pressure area over the
East Central Bay of Bengal is expected to intensify into a depression, a deep depression and
subsequently a cyclonic storm by day after tomorrow.
The state government has placed disaster response teams on standby, raided cyclone shelters,
and directed district administrations to remain alert.
Schools, colleges, and Yanganwadi centers in Ganjaham, Gajapati, Rai Gada, Koraput
and Balkan Giri will remain closed on Wednesday and Thursday.
As a precaution, two gates of the Indrapati Reservoir in Navrangpur district have also
been opened in anticipation of heavy rainfall.
The government is aiming for zero casualties and has urged people to follow official weather
advisories.
Prakash Das for Akashwani News, Bhuvaneshwar.
IMD has issued a red-collar warning for heavy-to-very heavy rainfall, with isolated, extremely heavy
rainfall over Kerala, Mahayet, Tamil Nadu, Buddhicherry and Karahekal tomorrow.
Antamana, Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep and South interior Karnataka will experience
heavy rainfall tomorrow.
In men's cricket, India defeated hosts New Zealand by four wickets.
In the second T20 International in Christchurch, today to take a two-nil lead in the five-match series.
India achieved the target of 181 runs in 19.5 overs, losing six wickets.
For the visitors, Dilak Verma scored the highest, unbeaten at 51 runs of 26 balls.
Earlier, team India's bowlers restricted New Zealand to 180 runs for five wickets in 20 overs.
The Aichi Nagoya 2026 Asian Paragames concluded today, with a closing ceremony at the Mizu
or Park Athletic Stadium in Nagoya, Japan, double gold medalists Nishat Kumar and Monagar
were led the Indian contingent as flag bearers at the closing ceremony. Interfinished the
games with the record 114 medals, including 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze medals.
surpassing its previous tally of 108 medals at the 2023 Asian Paragames in Hangzhou, China.
A report.
Para athletes with 65 medals were India's biggest medal contributors.
They won 22 gold, 19 silver and 24 bronze.
Para badminton followed with 16 medals including 3 gold, 5 silver and 8 bronze.
India also secured 11 medals in para swimming, 7 in para table tennis,
6 in para archery, 5 in para shooting, and 2 each in para judo and para powerlifting.
The 6th edition of the Asian Para Games will be held in Doha in 2030, Amrit Bhushan sports
desk.
President Ropini Murmur has expressed joy and pride at the unprecedented success of
the Indian para-athletes.
In badminton to time, Olympic medalist BV Sindhu has entered the final of the French
open after defeating Japan's Hina Akechi in a hard-fought semi-final at the arena Grand Prix today.
And now, before we end the bulletin, the headlines once again.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi to share his thoughts in his monthly radio program,
